President Donald Trump signed Section 338 proclamations adding a 50 per cent tariff on covered Canadian goods from August 19.
The White House said covered goods remain liable even if they originate under USMCA, affecting apparel tariff certainty.
TexPro data shows US textile and apparel imports from Canada totalled $1.45 billion in CY 2025, including $519 million in apparel.

title: India’s structural challenges threaten 2047 goal; growth strong: WTO
summary:
India’s FY28 real GDP growth is projected to be 6.8-7.2 per cent, but sustaining the economic performance needed to turn developed by 2047 will need addressing structural challenges, including high trade costs, regulatory complexity, infrastructure gaps and barriers to deeper global integration, the WTO noted.
Use of non-tariff measures by some nations has constrained market access for Indian exporters.

title: Vietnam calls for stronger ASEAN-US ties in trade, energy transition
summary:
Vietnam recently proposed expanding US-ASEAN cooperation in trade, investment, AI, semiconductors and clean energy as the two sides seek to deepen their Comprehensive Strategic Partnership. 
Vietnamese Foreign Minister Le Hoai Trung called for continued US support for Mekong sub-regional cooperation, particularly in water resource management, climate change adaptation and sustainable infrastructure.

title: Bangladesh PM forms committee to tackle textile sector issues
summary:
Bangladesh PM Tarique Rahman recently formed a high-level committee to review and resolve problems being faced by the country’s textile sector.
This followed a meeting between leaders from the Bangladesh Textile Mills Association (BTMA) and Rahman.
BTMA leaders sought the government’s continued support for the sector’s sustainable development and urged policy support to enhance its global competitiveness.

title: India's cotton risk builds as sowing lags and ICE rises
summary:
India’s kharif cotton sowing was 5.97 per cent behind last year at 92.53 lakh hectares as of July 17, with delayed rains affecting key states.
ICE December 2026 cotton rose to 80.42 cents per pound on July 21, adding to raw-material risk for mills.
Duty-free imports until October 31 may buffer mills, but yarn margins and sourcing costs remain exposed.

title: Dhaka plans to privatise petro products import, power distribution
summary:
Bangladesh is planning to allow the private sector to import petroleum products to reduce the subsidy burden, according to Energy and Mineral Resources Minister Iqbal Hasan Mahmud.
The government also plans to privatise power distribution for the same reason, he told a recent discussion on energy security.
His ministry has invited private sector proposals to take over electricity distribution companies.

title: UK shelf gaps widen as Middle East tensions disrupt trade: Survey
summary:
Global supply chain disruption linked to Middle East tensions is affecting product availability across the UK.
More than half of shoppers have noticed worsening shelf availability, while grocery and fashion stockouts are prompting consumers to switch retailers, brands and shopping channels.
The findings highlight growing pressure on retailers to strengthen inventory planning and product availability.

title: EU, Euro area fiscal deficit narrows to 3.1% of GDP in Q1
summary:
The euro area and the European Union each recorded a seasonally adjusted government deficit-to-GDP ratio of 3.1 per cent in the first quarter of 2026, down from 3.2 per cent and 3.4 per cent, respectively, in the previous quarter, Eurostat said. 
The improvement came as both government revenue and expenditure, measured as shares of GDP, edged lower across the two regions.

title: Bulgaria's apparel exports extend fourth year of decline
summary:
Bulgaria's apparel exports fell 19.9 per cent year on year to $254.56 million in Q1 2026, extending a multi-year decline from the 2022 peak amid weaker European demand and shifting sourcing patterns.
Germany remained the largest export market, followed by France and Italy.
Cotton apparel dominated exports, while trousers and shorts remained the country's leading apparel export category.

title: Is China+1 dead? How FTAs give India a second chance
summary:
Chief mentor of CMAI, Rahul Mehta said India captured only limited gains from the China+1 sourcing shift as buyers sought greater scale, while Bangladesh and Vietnam advanced faster. 
With apparel exports at $16.29 billion last year and $4.19 billion in Q1 2026, FTAs offer fresh opportunities, but compliance, labour, quality and scale remain key hurdles.

title: US apparel importers face brief tariff window before section 301
summary:
US apparel importers may see a roughly 48-hour tariff gap as the 10 per cent Section 122 surcharge is scheduled to expire on July 24, 2026.
A proposed Section 301 duty of 10 per cent or 12.5 per cent on imports from 60 economies has not yet been finalised.
Customs-entry timing will be critical for landed-cost planning and shipment release.

title: India’s Arvind Fashions’ Q1 revenue jumps as direct sales strengthen
summary:
India's Arvind Fashions Ltd has reported a 15.5 per cent YoY rise in Q1 FY27 revenue to ₹1,279 crore (~$127.9 million), driven by strong direct-to-consumer channel growth. 
EBITDA increased 19.6 per cent, while PAT declined due to lower other income. 
The company expects 12-15 per cent revenue growth in FY27 supported by retail expansion, AI adoption and operational efficiencies.

title: DGFT's RCMC relief proposal limited by ₹10,000 shipment cap
summary:
India's DGFT has proposed waiving RCMC for postal, courier and e-commerce export consignments with FOB value up to ₹10,000 (~$115).
The move cuts a fixed compliance cost for micro-exporters, but the low cap may limit any lift for apparel exporters using FTP benefits.
Stakeholders seek a turnover-based route and safeguards before consultation closes on July 30, 2026.

title: EU’s €750 mn crackdown puts China’s $42 bn apparel trade on notice
summary:
European Commission penalties totalling €750 million (~$857 million) against AliExpress and Temu push online fashion compliance upstream from parcels to platforms.
TexPro says extra-EU apparel imports from China rose 17.10 per cent to $42.09 billion in 2025, lifting share to 29.03 per cent.
Sellers and sourcing teams face scrutiny over listing data, seller identities and tariff classifications.

title: Jordan invites US apparel firms to explore investment opportunities
summary:
Jordanian Minister of Industry, Trade and Supply Yarub Qudah recently discussed with American Apparel and Footwear Association (AAFA) representatives strengthening trade cooperation and exploring opportunities to attract new investments to Jordan. 
The discussions took place in Washington during a session hosted by AAFA. 
Qudah invited US companies to explore investment opportunities in Jordan.

title: Nepalese PM takes steps to revive garment industry
summary:
Following a recent meeting with representatives from the Garment Association Nepal, PM Balendra Shah has instructed ministries to clear pending administrative delays, form a dedicated Textile and Clothing Development Council and restart factories closed for long. 
The Ministry of Foreign Affairs has been asked to resolve laboratory testing hurdles that have restricted exports to the US.

title: UV-resistant and fan-powered: India's next performance fabric frontier
summary:
Zeel Climate Clothing has shown summer apparel prototypes at Bharat Tex 2026 using UV-resistant, heat-resistant and moisture-absorbent synthetic fabric with fan-assisted air circulation.
The India-focused launch signals growing demand for functional fashion as heatwaves reshape clothing needs.
Zeel is selling direct-to-consumer first, with scale-up planned after consumer response data.

title: New Zealand apparel imports fall to $603 mn in H1 2026
summary:
New Zealand's apparel imports fell 3.2 per cent year on year to NZ$1.03 billion (~$603.5 million) in January-June 2026, reflecting cautious consumer demand and disciplined retailer inventories, despite a modest recovery in June.
Meanwhile, apparel exports rose 5.8 per cent in the first half and 28.9 per cent in June, driven mainly by strong growth in knitted apparel exports.
